delivered_contract: Non-null name, membership, color and opacity always record one complete cluster_op v1 input, regardless of legacy commit/log flags. Pure pose preview remains unchanged; explicit pose confirm uses the same owned publication.

Creation and edits share lock-owned selection, early historical/loadout checks, detached native builder output, structural/member validation before publication, exact source/session/revision check and one rollback-safe undo/revision.

Typed member references reject missing, duplicate, repeated or ambiguous targets. IDs and collection counts are bounded before model parsing; request and exact emitted command fit the existing JSON operation envelope.
Membership dependencies read named helices, owning strands and topology, with a conservative barrier. Saved full-field pose rows are also barriers; old v1/v2 builder mathematics remain unchanged.

Membership/mixed authored-pose responses use accepted candidate geometry outside the publication lock, with the captured request revision. Client adoption handles design and geometry together and drops reversed stale responses. Name/style and gizmo pose-only commits stay lean.

Owned creation/edit response formatting disables legacy auto-membership inference in full, compact, partial and skip-geometry helper branches. Default inference remains unchanged for other legacy callers.

No full history proof, dependency indexing, atom traversal or reconciliation was added to drag previews. Models, numerical manifests, scientific constants and native geometry kernels were not changed.
remaining_limits: FH-18 remains open: typed incoming deletion owners, an explicit recorded group-removal lifecycle, seek without resurrection, placement-preserving regrouping/deletion and unsupported-combination refusal, cluster-unassigned and duplex rotation-point authoring.
Pose-only previews still mutate compatibility state silently. Private ownership, cancel and undo lifecycle remain FH-23.
Whole-design undo copying and duplicate bounded member lookups under the lock require actual-workload timing. Unit durations do not qualify responsiveness.

Accepted compatibility Designs remain mutable. Holding their reference outside the lock protects against replacement, not arbitrary in-place legacy mutation. Immutable-host qualification remains FH-28.
Native response geometry/serialization runs after commit; failure there does not roll back the accepted edit. This follows existing response behavior and is not a claim of whole-HTTP rollback.
Standalone geometry GETs and older-server fallback lack a general revision pairing contract (ISSUE-107, FH-27). The new embedded group response avoids that path; it does not repair every caller.
Rootless legacy input remains unverified; response suppression does not invent a recipe root or remove legacy inference from unrelated GETs.
